sentences.zh: 杜彥杜彥，雲中人也。

translations.literal: Du Yan—Du Yan was a native of Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yan was from Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 父遷，屬葛榮之亂，徙家於幽。

translations.literal: His father Qian, during Ge Rong's rebellion, moved the family to You.
translations.idiomatic: During Ge Rong's rebellion, his father Qian relocated the household to Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 彥性勇果，善騎射。

translations.literal: Yan by nature was brave and resolute, skilled in mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was bold and decisive by nature and excelled at horseback archery.

sentences.zh: 仕周，釋褐左侍上士，後從柱國陸通擊陳將吳明徹於土州，破之。

translations.literal: He served Zhou, upon first appointment becoming Left Attendant Senior Clerk; later he followed the pillar of state Lu Tong in attacking the Chen general Wu Mingche at Tuzhou and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Zhou service as Left Attendant Senior Clerk and later followed Pillar of State Lu Tong to attack the Chen general Wu Mingche at Tuzhou and rout him.

sentences.zh: 又擊叛蠻，克倉塠、白楊二柵，並斬其渠帥。

translations.literal: He again attacked rebel barbarians, captured the two stockades of Cangdui and Baiyang, and beheaded their chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: He also campaigned against rebel tribes, took the stockades at Cangdui and Baiyang, and executed their leaders.

sentences.zh: 進平郢州賊帥樊志，以戰功拜大都督。

translations.literal: Advancing, he pacified the Yingzhou bandit leader Fan Zhi and, for battle merit, was appointed Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to suppress the Yingzhou rebel Fan Zhi and, for his victories, was appointed Grand Commander.

sentences.zh: 尋遷儀同，治隆山郡事。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Palace Attendant of the First Rank and administered the affairs of Longshan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Palace Attendant of the First Rank and put in charge of Longshan commandery.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜隴州刺史，賜爵永安縣伯。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed prefect of Longzhou and ennobled as Baron of Yong'an county.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became prefect of Longzhou and was created Baron of Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，從韋孝寬擊尉迥於相州，每戰有功，賜物三千段，奴婢三十口。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu was chief minister, he followed Wei Xiaokuan in attacking Yuwen Yong at Xiangzhou; in every battle he had merit, and was granted three thousand bolts of goods and thirty household slaves.
translations.idiomatic: While Gaozu was still chief minister, he followed Wei Xiaokuan against Yuwen Yong at Xiangzhou, distinguishing himself in every engagement and receiving three thousand bolts of goods and thirty slaves.

sentences.zh: 進位上開府，改封襄武縣侯，拜魏郡太守。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Senior Commander-in-Chief, his fief changed to Marquis of Xiangwu county, and he was appointed administrator of Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Senior Commander-in-Chief, enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiangwu, and appointed administrator of Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，授丹州刺史，進爵為公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was appointed prefect of Danzhou and advanced in rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaihuang era he was made prefect of Danzhou and raised to ducal rank.

sentences.zh: 後六歲，征為左武衛將軍。

translations.literal: Six years later he was summoned to serve as general of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Six years later he was recalled to the capital as general of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 平陳之役，以行軍總管與新義公韓擒相繼而進。

translations.literal: In the campaign to pacify Chen, as campaign commander he advanced in succession with the Duke of Xinyi, Han Qin.
translations.idiomatic: During the conquest of Chen he served as campaign commander, advancing in concert with Duke of Xinyi Han Qin.

sentences.zh: 軍至南陵，賊屯據江岸，彥遣儀同樊子蓋率精兵擊破其柵，獲船六百餘艘。

translations.literal: When the army reached Nanling, the enemy held the riverbank; Yan sent Palace Attendant Fan Zigai at the head of picked troops to smash their palisade and seize more than six hundred boats.
translations.idiomatic: At Nanling the enemy held the riverbank; Yan sent Palace Attendant Fan Zigai with an elite force to break their stockade and capture more than six hundred vessels.

sentences.zh: 渡江，擊南陵城，拔之，擒其守將許翼。

translations.literal: Crossing the river, he attacked Nanling city, took it, and captured its defending general Xu Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Yangzi, stormed Nanling, took the city, and captured its commander Xu Yi.

sentences.zh: 進至新林，與擒合軍。

translations.literal: Advancing to Xinlin, he united his forces with Qin's.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed on to Xinlin and joined forces with Han Qin.

sentences.zh: 及陳平，賜物五千段，粟六千石，進位柱國，賜子寶安爵昌陽縣公。

translations.literal: When Chen was pacified, he was granted five thousand bolts of goods and six thousand piculs of grain, advanced to Pillar of State, and his son Bao'an was ennobled as Duke of Changyang county.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen fell he received five thousand bolts of goods and six thousand piculs of grain, was promoted to Pillar of State, and his son Bao'an was created Duke of Changyang.

sentences.zh: 高智慧等之作亂也，複以行軍總管從楊素討之，別解江州圍。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhihui and others rose in rebellion, he again served as campaign commander following Yang Su to suppress them and separately lifted the siege of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhihui and others rebelled, he again served as campaign commander under Yang Su and on his own broke the siege of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 智慧餘黨往往屯聚，保投溪洞，彥水陸兼進，攻錦山、陽父、若、石壁四洞，悉平之，皆斬其渠帥。

translations.literal: Zhihui's remaining partisans often gathered and took refuge in stream caves; Yan advanced by land and water, attacked the four lairs of Jinshan, Yangfu, Ruo, and Shibi, pacified them all, and beheaded their chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: Zhihui's scattered followers held out in mountain ravines; Yan struck by land and water, reduced the strongholds at Jinshan, Yangfu, Ruo, and Shibi, and executed their leaders.

sentences.zh: 賊李陀擁眾數千，據彭山，彥襲擊破之，斬陀，傳其首。

translations.literal: The bandit Li Tuo mustered several thousand men and held Pengshan; Yan raided and defeated him, beheaded Tuo, and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Li Tuo gathered several thousand men on Pengshan; Yan surprised and routed him, killed Tuo, and forwarded his head.

sentences.zh: 又擊徐州、宜豐二洞，悉平之。

translations.literal: He again attacked the two lairs of Xuzhou and Yifeng and pacified them completely.
translations.idiomatic: He also subdued the rebel bases at Xuzhou and Yifeng.

sentences.zh: 賜奴婢百餘口。

translations.literal: He was granted more than a hundred household slaves.
translations.idiomatic: He was rewarded with more than a hundred slaves.

sentences.zh: 拜洪州總管，甚有治名。

translations.literal: He was appointed regional commander of Hongzhou and gained a great reputation for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed regional commander of Hongzhou, he earned a strong reputation for effective administration.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，雲州總管賀婁子幹卒，上悼惜者久之，因謂侍臣曰：「榆林國之重鎮，安得子幹之輩乎？

translations.literal: After more than a year, Yunzhou regional commander Helou Zigan died; the emperor mourned him for a long time and said to his attendants: "Yulin is a vital fortress of the state—where can we find men like Zigan?
translations.idiomatic: A year later Yunzhou commander Helou Zigan died. The emperor grieved for him at length and told his courtiers, "Yulin is a strategic bulwark of the realm—where shall we find another man like Zigan?

sentences.zh: 」後數日，上曰：「吾思可以鎮榆林者，莫過杜彥。

translations.literal: " Several days later the emperor said: "When I consider who could guard Yulin, none surpasses Du Yan.
translations.idiomatic: " A few days later he said, "When I think who should hold Yulin, no one surpasses Du Yan.

sentences.zh: 」於是征拜雲州總管。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was summoned and appointed regional commander of Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " He was then recalled and appointed regional commander of Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 突厥來寇，彥輒擒斬之，北夷畏憚，胡馬不敢至塞。

translations.literal: When the Turks came to raid, Yan would capture and behead them; the northern barbarians feared him, and Turkic horses dared not approach the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Turks raided, Yan captured and executed them; the northern peoples stood in awe of him, and their horsemen no longer dared approach the border.

sentences.zh: 後數年，朝廷複追錄前功，賜子寶虔爵承縣公。

translations.literal: Several years later the court again recorded his earlier merit and ennobled his son Baoqian as Duke of Cheng county.
translations.idiomatic: Some years later the court posthumously recognized his earlier service and created his son Baoqian Duke of Cheng.

sentences.zh: 十八年，遼東之役，以行軍總管從漢王至營州。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, in the Liaodong campaign, as campaign commander he followed the Prince of Han to Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year eighteen of the Liaodong campaign he served as campaign commander under the Prince of Han and marched to Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 上以彥曉習軍旅，令總統五十營事。

translations.literal: Because the emperor knew Yan was versed in military affairs, he ordered him to oversee the affairs of fifty camps.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Yan's mastery of military affairs, the emperor put him in overall charge of fifty camps.

sentences.zh: 及還，拜朔州總管。

translations.literal: Upon his return he was appointed regional commander of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed regional commander of Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 突厥複寇雲州，上令楊素擊走之，是後猶恐為邊患，以彥素為突厥所憚，複拜雲州總管。

translations.literal: The Turks again raided Yunzhou; the emperor ordered Yang Su to drive them off. Still fearing border trouble afterward, and because Yan had long been feared by the Turks, he was again appointed regional commander of Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks raided Yunzhou again, the emperor sent Yang Su to repel them; still anxious about the frontier, and knowing the Turks feared Yan, he reappointed him commander of Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以疾征還，卒，時年六十。

translations.literal: Before long, recalled on account of illness, he died at the age of sixty.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was recalled because of illness and died at sixty.

sentences.zh: 子寶虔，大業末，文城郡丞。

translations.literal: His son Baoqian, at the end of the Daye era, was assistant administrator of Wencheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Baoqian served late in the Daye era as assistant administrator of Wencheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 高勱高勱，字敬德，渤海蓚人也，齊太尉、清河王嶽之子也。

translations.literal: Gao Mai—Gao Mai, courtesy name Jingde, was a native of Tiao in Bohai, son of Qi Grand Marshal and Prince of Qinghe, Gao Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Mai, courtesy name Jingde, was from Tiao in Bohai, the son of Qi Grand Marshal and Prince of Qinghe Gao Yue.

sentences.zh: 幼聰敏，美風儀，以仁孝聞，為齊顯祖所愛。

translations.literal: As a child he was clever, of fine bearing, renowned for benevolence and filial piety, and beloved by Emperor Xianzu of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he was quick-witted and handsome, famed for kindness and filial devotion, and a favorite of Qi Emperor Xianzu.

sentences.zh: 年七歲，襲爵清河王。

translations.literal: At age seven he inherited the title Prince of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he inherited the title Prince of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 十四為青州刺史，曆右衛將軍、領軍大將軍、祠部尚書、開府儀同三司，改封樂安王。

translations.literal: At fourteen he became prefect of Qingzhou, and successively served as general of the Right Guard, commander of the Palace Guard, minister of the Directorate of Sacrifices, and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon; his fief was changed to Prince of Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he was made prefect of Qingzhou and later held posts as general of the Right Guard, commander of the Palace Guard, minister of sacrifices, and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, eventually being enfeoffed as Prince of Le'an.

sentences.zh: 性剛直，有才幹，甚為時人所重。

translations.literal: By nature he was upright and firm, talented and capable, and greatly respected by men of his time.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and capable by nature, he was widely esteemed in his day.

sentences.zh: 斛律明月雅敬之，每有征伐，則引之為副。

translations.literal: Hulü Mingyue held him in high esteem; whenever there was a campaign, he would take Mai as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Hulü Mingyue admired him greatly and always took him as second-in-command on campaign.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中、尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Attendant and Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Palace Attendant and Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 及後主為周師所敗，勱奉太后歸鄴。

translations.literal: When the Later Ruler was defeated by Zhou troops, Mai escorted the empress dowager back to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Ruler was routed by Zhou forces, Mai escorted the empress dowager back to Ye.

sentences.zh: 時宦官放縱，儀同苟子溢尤稱寵倖，勱將斬之以徇。

translations.literal: At the time eunuchs ran rampant; Palace Attendant Gou Ziyi was especially favored, and Mai was about to behead him as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs were running wild at court; Palace Attendant Gou Ziyi was a particular favorite, and Mai was on the point of executing him as an example.

sentences.zh: 太后救之，乃釋。

translations.literal: The empress dowager rescued him, and Mai released him.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager intervened and Mai let him go.

sentences.zh: 劉文殊竊謂勱曰：「子溢之徒，言成禍福，何得如此！

translations.literal: Liu Wenshu privately said to Mai: "Men like Ziyi can make fortune or ruin with a word—how can you act like this!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wenshu whispered to Mai, "Men like Ziyi can make or break you with a word—how can you go so far!

sentences.zh: 」勱攘袂曰：「今者西寇日侵，朝貴多叛，正由此輩弄權，致使衣冠解體。

translations.literal: " Mai rolled up his sleeves and said: "Now the western enemy presses daily, and many court nobles have defected—precisely because this lot manipulate power and have brought the ruling class to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: " Mai flung up his sleeves and said, "The western foe advances daily and great families are defecting—because men like these abuse power and have torn the court apart.

sentences.zh: 若得今日殺之，明日受誅，無所恨也。

translations.literal: If I could kill him today and be executed tomorrow, I would have no regret.
translations.idiomatic: If I could kill him today and die tomorrow, I would not regret it.

sentences.zh: 」文殊甚愧。

translations.literal: " Wenshu was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: " Wenshu was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 既至鄴，勱勸後主：「五品已上家累，悉置三台之上，因脅之曰：'若戰不捷，則燒之。

translations.literal: When they reached Ye, Mai advised the Later Ruler: "Place the families of all officials of the fifth rank and above on the Three Platforms, and threaten them, saying: 'If the battle is not won, they will be burned.
translations.idiomatic: Once in Ye, Mai urged the Later Ruler: "Gather the families of every official of the fifth rank and above on the Three Platforms and tell them, 'If we do not win, we burn them.

sentences.zh: '此輩惜妻子，必當死戰，可敗也。

translations.literal: ' These men cherish wife and children and will surely fight to the death—the enemy can be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: ' They love their wives and children and will fight to the death—we can defeat the enemy.

sentences.zh: 」後主不從，遂棄鄴東遁。

translations.literal: " The Later Ruler would not follow this advice and abandoned Ye, fleeing east.
translations.idiomatic: " The Later Ruler refused, abandoned Ye, and fled east.

sentences.zh: 勱恆後殿，為周軍所得。

translations.literal: Mai always brought up the rear and was captured by Zhou troops.
translations.idiomatic: Mai always commanded the rearguard and was captured by Zhou forces.

sentences.zh: 武帝見之，與語，大悅，因問齊亡所由。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou saw him, spoke with him, and was greatly pleased; he then asked the cause of Qi's fall.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou met him, spoke with him, and was delighted; he then asked why Qi had perished.

sentences.zh: 勱發言流涕，悲不自勝，帝亦為之改容。

translations.literal: As Mai spoke he wept, overcome with grief; the emperor too changed countenance for his sake.
translations.idiomatic: Mai spoke through tears, overcome with grief, and the emperor's expression softened in sympathy.

sentences.zh: 授開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，謂勱曰：「齊所以亡者，由任邪佞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu was chief minister, he said to Mai: "Qi perished because it employed wicked flatterers.
translations.idiomatic: While Gaozu was still chief minister, he told Mai, "Qi fell because it trusted wicked flatterers.

sentences.zh: 公父子忠良，聞於鄰境，宜善自愛。

translations.literal: Your father and you are loyal and good, renowned in neighboring states—you should take good care of yourselves.
translations.idiomatic: Your house is known beyond the borders for loyalty—take good care of yourselves.

sentences.zh: 」勱再拜謝曰：「勱亡齊末屬，世荷恩榮，不能扶危定傾，以致淪覆。

translations.literal: " Mai bowed twice and replied: "Mai is a remnant subject of fallen Qi; my house has long received favor and glory, yet I could not shore up peril and steady the tipping state, and so ruin came.
translations.idiomatic: " Mai bowed deeply and said, "I am a remnant of fallen Qi; my family long enjoyed imperial favor, yet I could not save the state from collapse.

sentences.zh: 既蒙獲宥，恩幸已多，況複濫叨名位，致速官謗。

translations.literal: Having been spared, I have already received excessive grace; how much more if I undeservedly accept rank and office and hasten official censure.
translations.idiomatic: I have already been shown more mercy than I deserve; to accept office on top of that would only invite reproach.

sentences.zh: 」高祖甚器之，以勱檢校揚州事。

translations.literal: " Gaozu thought highly of him and put Mai in charge of Yangzhou affairs on probation.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu esteemed him greatly and placed him in provisional charge of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 後拜楚州刺史，民安之。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed prefect of Chuzhou, and the people were at peace under him.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed prefect of Chuzhou, where the people lived in peace under his rule.

sentences.zh: 先是，城北有伍子胥廟，其俗敬鬼。

translations.literal: Earlier, north of the city wall there was a temple to Wu Zixu; the local custom was to revere spirits.
translations.idiomatic: North of the city stood a temple to Wu Zixu, and the people were devoted to spirit worship.

sentences.zh: 祈禱者必以牛酒，至破產業。

translations.literal: Those who prayed had to offer cattle and wine, even to the ruin of their households.
translations.idiomatic: Worshippers had to sacrifice cattle and wine, often until their families were ruined.

sentences.zh: 勱歎曰：「子胥賢者，豈宜損百姓乎？

translations.literal: Mai sighed and said: "Zixu was a worthy man—how could he wish to harm the common people?
translations.idiomatic: Mai sighed and said, "Zixu was a worthy man—would he want the people ruined?

sentences.zh: 」乃告諭所部，自此遂止，百姓賴之。

translations.literal: " He then issued proclamations throughout his jurisdiction; from then on the practice ceased, and the people were indebted to him.
translations.idiomatic: " He issued orders throughout his district, the practice stopped, and the people were grateful.

sentences.zh: 七年，轉光州刺史，上取陳五策，又上表曰：「臣聞夷凶翦暴，王者之懋功；

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to be prefect of Guangzhou; he submitted five stratagems against Chen and also memorialized: "Your servant has heard that cutting down barbarian foes and eliminating the violent is the king's great merit;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he became prefect of Guangzhou, submitted five plans against Chen, and memorialized: "I have heard that subduing barbarian violence is the supreme achievement of a true king;

sentences.zh: 取亂侮亡，往賢之雅誥。

translations.literal: to take advantage of disorder and insult the perishing is the elegant admonition of former worthies.
translations.idiomatic: and that striking a tottering foe is the counsel of the ancient sages.

sentences.zh: 是以苗民逆命，爰興兩階之舞；

translations.literal: Therefore when the Miao people defied orders, the dance of the two staircases was performed;
translations.idiomatic: When the Miao rebelled, the dance of the two courts was staged;

sentences.zh: 有扈不賓，終召六師之伐。

translations.literal: when Youhu failed to submit, in the end the six armies were summoned to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: when Youhu refused allegiance, the six hosts were finally sent against them.

sentences.zh: 皆所以寧一宇內，匡濟群生者也。

translations.literal: All these were means to pacify the realm under heaven and succor the multitude of living beings.
translations.idiomatic: All to bring peace under heaven and deliver the people.

sentences.zh: 自昔晉氏失馭，天網絕維，群凶於焉蝟起，三方因而鼎立。

translations.literal: Since olden days when the Jin house lost the reins, heaven's net was torn and the cords broken; many villains rose like hedgehogs, and the three regions accordingly stood like a tripod.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since the Jin lost control and order collapsed, rebels sprang up everywhere and three kingdoms stood in rivalry.

sentences.zh: 陳氏乘其際運，拔起細微，茜頊縱其長蛇，竊據吳會；

translations.literal: The Chen house seized this opportune fortune, rising from humble origins; Chen Qian stretched out like a long serpent and stealthily held Wu and Kuaiji;
translations.idiomatic: The house of Chen seized its moment, rising from obscurity; Chen Qian extended his power like a great serpent and seized Wu and Kuaiji;

sentences.zh: 叔寶肆其昏虐，毒被金陵。

translations.literal: Chen Shubao indulged his benighted cruelty, and poison spread over Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shubao gave free rein to folly and cruelty, and his poison spread through Jinling.

sentences.zh: 數年已來，荒悖滋甚。

translations.literal: For several years now, wild perversity has grown ever worse.
translations.idiomatic: For years his excesses have grown worse.

sentences.zh: 牝雞司旦，昵近奸回，尚方役徒，積骸千數，疆埸防守，長戍三年。

translations.literal: A hen crows at dawn; he draws close to wicked schemers; convict laborers of the imperial workshops pile up by the thousands; frontier defense keeps men on long garrison for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Women rule at court, villains are his intimates, imperial workshops pile up thousands of corpses, and frontier troops serve three-year tours.

sentences.zh: 或微行暴露，沉湎王侯之宅；

translations.literal: At times he goes abroad incognito in revealing dress, drowning himself in the mansions of princes and marquises;
translations.idiomatic: He wanders abroad in disguise, debauching himself in the houses of nobles;

sentences.zh: 或賓士駿騎，顛墜康衢之首。

translations.literal: or with guest knights and swift steeds he tumbles at the head of the broad highway.
translations.idiomatic: or gallops with rowdy companions until he falls in the public streets.

sentences.zh: 有功不賞，無辜獲戮，烽燧日警，未以為虞，耽淫靡嫚，不知紀極。

translations.literal: Merit goes unrewarded, the innocent are put to death; beacon fires warn daily, yet he is not alarmed; sunk in lust and dissipation, he knows no limit.
translations.idiomatic: The worthy go unrewarded and the innocent are killed; beacon fires blaze daily yet he feels no alarm; sunk in debauchery, he knows no bounds.

sentences.zh: 天厭亂德，妖實人興，或空裡時有大聲，或行路共傳鬼怪，或刳人肝以祠天狗，或自捨身以厭妖訛。

translations.literal: Heaven loathes chaotic virtue; portents arise and men stir—sometimes great sounds in the empty air, sometimes travelers all report ghosts and monsters, sometimes human livers are cut out to sacrifice to the celestial dog, sometimes men give up their own bodies to appease strange calamities.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven rejects his misrule: omens multiply—strange cries in the sky, ghosts reported on every road, livers cut out to appease the celestial dog, men offering their own lives to ward off evil.

sentences.zh: 民神怨憤，災異薦發，天時人事，昭然可知。

translations.literal: The people and the spirits are resentful and angry; disasters and anomalies arise in succession—the signs of heaven and the affairs of men are plainly evident.
translations.idiomatic: People and spirits alike are enraged; disasters follow one after another—the judgment of heaven is plain for all to see.

sentences.zh: 臣以庸才，猥蒙朝寄，頻曆籓任，與其鄰接，密邇仇讎，知其動靜，天討有罪，此即其時。

translations.literal: Your servant, with mediocre talent, has undeservedly received the court's trust, repeatedly holding frontier posts bordering Chen, close to this enemy, and knows their movements; heaven's punishment of the guilty—this is the moment.
translations.idiomatic: I am but a mediocre man who has undeservedly held posts on Chen's border and know their movements well; heaven's punishment of the guilty has come—now is the time.

sentences.zh: 若戎車雷動，戈船電邁，臣難驚怯，請效鷹犬。

translations.literal: If war chariots thunder forth and armed ships flash forward, though your servant is hardly bold, I beg to serve like hawk and hound.
translations.idiomatic: When the army marches and the fleet strikes, though I am no bold warrior, I beg to serve as your hunting dog.

sentences.zh: 」高祖覽表嘉之，答以優詔。

translations.literal: " Gaozu read the memorial with approval and replied with an excellent edict.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu read the memorial with approval and answered with a gracious edict.

sentences.zh: 及大舉伐陳，以勱為行軍總管，從宜陽公王世積下陳江州。

translations.literal: When the great campaign against Chen was launched, Mai served as campaign commander, following the Duke of Yiyang, Wang Shiji, in descending on Chen's Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the great campaign against Chen he served as campaign commander under Duke of Yiyang Wang Shiji and advanced on Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以功拜上開府，賜物三千段。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed Senior Commander-in-Chief and granted three thousand bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made Senior Commander-in-Chief and given three thousand bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 隴右諸羌數為寇亂，朝廷以勱有威名，拜洮州刺史。

translations.literal: The Qiang of Longyou often raided and rebelled; the court, because Mai had a formidable reputation, appointed him prefect of Taozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang of Longyou raided repeatedly, and the court appointed Mai prefect of Taozhou for his renown.

sentences.zh: 下車大崇威惠，民夷悅附，其山谷間生羌相率詣府稱謁，前後至者，數千餘戶。

translations.literal: Upon taking office he greatly promoted authority and kindness; Chinese and barbarians gladly submitted, and raw Qiang from the mountain valleys came in groups to the prefecture to pay homage—more than several thousand households in all.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he combined firmness with kindness; Chinese and tribesmen alike submitted gladly, and Qiang from the valleys came in groups to pay homage—several thousand households in all.

sentences.zh: 豪猾屏跡，路不拾遺，在職數年，稱為治理。

translations.literal: The powerful and cunning vanished from sight; no one picked up lost goods on the road; during several years in office he was praised for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Lawless elements disappeared, lost goods went untouched on the roads, and after several years he was praised as an excellent administrator.

sentences.zh: 後遇吐谷渾來寇，勱遇疾不能拒戰，賊遂大掠而去。

translations.literal: Later when Tuyuhun came to raid, Mai fell ill and could not resist; the enemy plundered heavily and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Tuyuhun invaded, Mai was ill and unable to fight; the enemy looted extensively and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 憲司奏勱亡失戶口，又言受羌饋遺，竟坐免官。

translations.literal: The inspectorate memorialized that Mai had lost registered households and also said he had accepted gifts from the Qiang; in the end he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: The inspectorate charged him with losing registered population and accepting Qiang bribes, and he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 後卒于家，時年五十六。

translations.literal: Later he died at home at the age of fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He later died at home at the age of fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 子士廉，最知名。

translations.literal: His son Shilian was the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shilian became the most famous of his descendants.

sentences.zh: 爾朱敞爾硃敞，字乾羅，秀容契胡人，爾硃榮之族子也。

translations.literal: Erzhu Chang—Erzhu Chang, courtesy name Qianluo, was a man of the Qihu tribe of Xiurong, a clansman of Erzhu Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Chang, courtesy name Qianluo, was a Qihu tribesman of Xiurong and a kinsman of Erzhu Rong.

sentences.zh: 父彥伯，官至司徒、博陵王。

translations.literal: His father Yanbo rose to Grand Minister of State and Prince of Boling.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yanbo rose to Grand Minister of State and Prince of Boling.

sentences.zh: 齊神武帝韓陵之捷，盡誅爾硃氏，敞小，隨母養于宮中。

translations.literal: After Emperor Shenwu of Qi's victory at Hanling, the entire Erzhu clan was executed; Chang was young and was raised in the palace with his mother.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi Emperor Shenwu's victory at Hanling the Erzhu clan was wiped out; Chang was still a child and was raised in the palace with his mother.

sentences.zh: 及年十二，自竇而走，至於大街，見童兒群戲者，敞解所著綺羅金翠之服，易衣而遁。

translations.literal: At age twelve he fled through a hole in the wall to the main street, saw children playing in a group, stripped off his brocade robes adorned with gold and kingfisher feathers, exchanged clothes, and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he slipped out through a hole in the wall onto the main street, saw children at play, stripped off his brocade and jeweled finery, traded clothes with one of them, and fled.

sentences.zh: 追騎尋至，初不識敞，便執綺衣兒。

translations.literal: Pursuers soon arrived; at first they did not recognize Chang and seized the child in brocade.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuers soon caught up; they did not recognize Chang at first and seized the child in brocade instead.

sentences.zh: 比究問知非，會日已暮，由是得免。

translations.literal: When questioning revealed their mistake, night had already fallen, and so he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Once questioning showed their mistake, night had fallen, and Chang got away.

sentences.zh: 遂入一村，見長孫氏媼踞胡床而坐。

translations.literal: He then entered a village and saw an old woman of the Zhangsun clan seated on a camp chair.
translations.idiomatic: He came to a village where an old woman of the Zhangsun clan sat on a camp stool.

sentences.zh: 敞再拜求哀，長孫氏湣之，藏於複壁。

translations.literal: Chang bowed twice and begged for pity; the Zhangsun woman took pity on him and hid him in a double wall.
translations.idiomatic: Chang bowed and pleaded for mercy; she pitied him and hid him in a secret compartment of the wall.

sentences.zh: 三年，購之愈急，跡且至，長孫氏曰：「事急矣，不可久留。

translations.literal: After three years the search grew ever more urgent and his trail was nearly found; the Zhangsun woman said: "The matter is urgent—you cannot stay long.
translations.idiomatic: After three years the manhunt intensified and pursuers were closing in; the Zhangsun woman said, "This has become urgent—you cannot stay here any longer.

sentences.zh: 」資而遣之。

translations.literal: " She supplied him with funds and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: " She gave him supplies and sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 遂詐為道士，變姓名，隱嵩山，略涉經史。

translations.literal: He then pretended to be a Daoist priest, changed his name, hid on Mount Song, and briefly studied the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: He disguised himself as a Daoist priest, took a new name, and lived in seclusion on Mount Song, where he read a little in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 數年之間，人頗異之。

translations.literal: Within a few years people found him rather unusual.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years people began to regard him as remarkable.

sentences.zh: 嘗獨坐岩石之下，泫然而歎曰：「吾豈終於此乎？

translations.literal: Once, sitting alone beneath a rock, he wept and sighed: "Am I to end my days like this?
translations.idiomatic: Once, sitting alone beneath a cliff, he wept and sighed, "Am I to end my days like this?

sentences.zh: 伍子胥獨何人也！

translations.literal: What sort of man was Wu Zixu alone!
translations.idiomatic: What was Wu Zixu, that he alone could rise so high!

sentences.zh: 」於是間行微服，西歸於周。

translations.literal: " He then traveled by secret routes in humble dress and returned west to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: " He then made his way west in disguise and returned to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 太祖見而禮之，拜大都督、行台郎中，封靈壽縣伯，邑千五百戶。

translations.literal: Grand Ancestor [Yuwen Tai] received him with ceremony, appointed him Grand Commander and Bureau Director of the Field Office, and enfeoffed him as Baron of Lingshou county with a fief of fifteen hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Ancestor Yuwen Tai received him with honor, made him Grand Commander and Bureau Director of the Field Office, and created him Baron of Lingshou with a fief of fifteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 遷通直散騎常侍，轉車騎大將軍、儀同三司，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant of the Unimpeded Cavalry, then made General of Chariots and Cavalry and Palace Attendant of the Third Rank, and advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Regular Attendant of the Unimpeded Cavalry, then made General of Chariots and Cavalry and Palace Attendant of the Third Rank, and raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 保定中，遷使持節、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: During Baoding he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, General of Agile Cavalry, and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: During the Baoding era he was made Bearer of the Staff, General of Agile Cavalry, and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 天和中，增邑五百戶，曆信、臨、熊、潼四州刺史，進爵為公。

translations.literal: During Tianhe his fief was increased by five hundred households; he served successively as prefect of Xin, Lin, Xiong, and Tong [prefectures], and advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianhe his fief grew by five hundred households; he served as prefect of Xin, Lin, Xiong, and Tong in turn, and was raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 武帝東征，上表求從，許之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu campaigned eastward, Chang memorialized asking to follow, and permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu marched east, Chang asked leave to accompany him and was permitted.

sentences.zh: 攻城陷陣，所當皆破，進位上開府。

translations.literal: In storming cities and breaking battle lines, wherever he faced the enemy he prevailed, and he was advanced to Senior Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In assaults on cities and charges through enemy lines he was invariably victorious and was promoted to Senior Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 除南光州刺史，入為護軍大將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed prefect of southern Guangzhou and then entered the capital as General of the Guard Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was made prefect of southern Guangzhou and later recalled to the capital as General of the Guard Army.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，轉膠州刺史。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to be prefect of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was transferred to Jiaozhou as prefect.

sentences.zh: 於是迎長孫氏及弟置於家，厚資給之。

translations.literal: He then welcomed the Zhangsun woman and his younger brother into his household and provided for them generously.
translations.idiomatic: He then brought the Zhangsun woman and his younger brother into his home and supported them generously.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，改封邊城郡公。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, Chang's fief was changed to Duke of Biancheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Chang was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Biancheng.

sentences.zh: 黔安蠻叛，命敞討平之。

translations.literal: The Qian'an barbarians rebelled, and Chang was ordered to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qian'an tribes rebelled, Chang was ordered to put them down.

sentences.zh: 師旋，拜金州總管。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was appointed regional commander of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed regional commander of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋轉徐州總管。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to regional commander of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to regional commander of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 在職數年，號為明肅，民吏懼之。

translations.literal: During several years in office he was known for clarity and severity, and officials and commoners alike feared him.
translations.idiomatic: After several years in office he was known for stern clarity, and both officials and commoners stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 後以年老，上表乞骸骨，賜二馬軺車，歸於河內，卒于家，時年七十二。

translations.literal: Later, on account of old age, he memorialized asking to retire; he was granted a two-horse light carriage, returned to Henei, and died at home at the age of seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he asked to retire; the court gave him a two-horse carriage, and he returned to Henei, where he died at seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 子最嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zui succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zui succeeded to his titles.

sentences.zh: 周搖周搖，字世安，其先與後魏同源，初為普乃氏，及居洛陽，改為周氏。

translations.literal: Zhou Yao—Zhou Yao, courtesy name Shi'an, was of the same origin as Later Wei; originally of the clan Punai, when they settled in Luoyang they changed to the surname Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yao, courtesy name Shi'an, shared origins with the Northern Wei; his clan was originally Punai, but after settling in Luoyang they took the surname Zhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖拔拔，祖右六肱，俱為北平王。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Baba and grandfather Youliugong were both Princes of Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Baba and grandfather Youliugong were both enfeoffed as Princes of Beiping.

sentences.zh: 父恕延，曆行台僕射、南荊州總管。

translations.literal: His father Shuyan successively served as Vice Director of the Field Office and regional commander of southern Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shuyan had served as Vice Director of the Field Office and regional commander of southern Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 搖少剛果，有武藝，性謹厚，動遵法度。

translations.literal: Yao in youth was firm and resolute, skilled in martial arts, of a cautious and honest nature, and in conduct always observed the law.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Yao was resolute and skilled in arms, cautious and honest by nature, and scrupulous in observing the law.

sentences.zh: 仕魏，官至開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He served Wei and rose to Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He served the Wei and rose to Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 周閔帝受禪，賜姓車非氏，封金水郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min of Zhou received the abdication, he was granted the surname Chefei and enfeoffed as Duke of Jinshui commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Emperor Min took the throne, Yao was granted the surname Chefei and created Duke of Jinshui.

sentences.zh: 曆夙、楚二州刺史，吏民安之。

translations.literal: He served successively as prefect of Su and Chu [prefectures], and officials and people were at peace under him.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Su and Chu in turn, and both officials and people lived in peace under his rule.

sentences.zh: 從帝平齊，每戰有功，超授柱國，進封夔國公。

translations.literal: Following the emperor in pacifying Qi, he had merit in every battle, was exceptionally appointed Pillar of State, and advanced to Duke of Kui.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the emperor in the conquest of Qi, distinguished himself in every battle, was made Pillar of State, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Kui.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜晉州總管。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed regional commander of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed regional commander of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 時高祖為定州總管，文獻皇后自京師詣高祖，路經搖所，主禮甚薄。

translations.literal: At the time Gaozu was regional commander of Dingzhou; Empress Wenxian came from the capital to visit Gaozu and passed through Yao's jurisdiction, where the reception he provided was very meager.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was then regional commander of Dingzhou; when Empress Wenxian traveled from the capital to visit him and passed through Yao's territory, Yao entertained her very sparingly.

sentences.zh: 既而白後曰：「公廨甚富於財，限法不敢輒費。

translations.literal: He then told the empress: "The government offices are very rich in funds, but the law sets limits and I dare not spend freely.
translations.idiomatic: He then told the empress, "My offices are well supplied with funds, but the law forbids me to spend them freely.

sentences.zh: 又王臣無得效私。

translations.literal: Moreover, as a king's minister one may not act out of private feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, a prince's minister must not indulge private favor.

sentences.zh: 」其質直如此。

translations.literal: " Such was his plain uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was his plain integrity.

sentences.zh: 高祖以其奉法，每嘉之。

translations.literal: Gaozu, because he upheld the law, always praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu admired him for his strict adherence to the law.

sentences.zh: 及為丞相，徙封濟北郡公，尋拜豫州總管。

translations.literal: When he became chief minister, Yao's fief was moved to Duke of Jibei commandery, and soon he was appointed regional commander of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu became chief minister, Yao was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Jibei and soon appointed regional commander of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，複姓周氏。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, Yao resumed the surname Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Yao resumed the surname Zhou.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，突厥寇邊，燕、薊多被其患，前總管李崇為虜所殺，上思所以鎮之，臨朝曰：「無以加周搖者。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang the Turks raided the frontier; Yan and Ji suffered heavily; the former commander Li Chong was killed by the enemy. The emperor considered how to secure the region and said at court: "None surpasses Zhou Yao for this post.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaihuang the Turks raided the frontier; Yan and Ji suffered greatly, and the former commander Li Chong was killed. The emperor sought someone to secure the region and declared at court, "No one surpasses Zhou Yao for this.

sentences.zh: 」拜為幽州總管六州五十鎮諸軍事。

translations.literal: " He was appointed regional commander of Youzhou with military authority over six prefectures and fifty garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: " He was appointed regional commander of Youzhou with authority over six prefectures and fifty garrisons.

sentences.zh: 搖修鄣塞，謹斥候，邊民以安。

translations.literal: Yao repaired border walls and stockades and kept watch posts strict; the frontier people were thereby secure.
translations.idiomatic: Yao repaired the border fortifications and kept watch posts alert, and the frontier people lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 後六載，徙為壽州。

translations.literal: Six years later he was transferred to Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Six years later he was transferred to Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，自以年老，乞骸骨，上召之。

translations.literal: Earlier, considering himself old, he had asked to retire; the emperor summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Having grown old, he had asked to retire; the emperor summoned him to court.

sentences.zh: 既引見，上勞之曰：「公積行累仁，曆仕三代，克終富貴，保茲遐壽，良足善也。

translations.literal: After he was received in audience, the emperor comforted him, saying: "Sir, you have accumulated conduct and heaped up benevolence, served through three dynasties, attained wealth and honor to the end, and preserved this long life—truly admirable.
translations.idiomatic: When he was received in audience, the emperor said to him, "You have lived a life of accumulated virtue, served three dynasties, kept your wealth and rank to the end, and enjoyed a long life—this is admirable indeed.

sentences.zh: 」賜坐褥，歸於第。

translations.literal: " He was granted a seat cushion and returned to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: " He was given a seat cushion and sent home to his estate.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，終於家，諡曰恭，時年八十四。

translations.literal: After more than a year he died at home; his posthumous title was Gong [Respectful], and he was eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he died at home and was given the posthumous title Gong; he was eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 獨孤楷獨孤楷，字修則，不知何許人也，本姓李氏。

translations.literal: Dugu Kai—Dugu Kai, courtesy name Xiuzi, was of unknown origin; his original surname was Li.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Kai, courtesy name Xiuzi, was of unknown origin and bore the surname Li by birth.

sentences.zh: 父屯，從齊神武帝與周師戰于沙苑，齊師敗績，因為柱國獨孤信所擒，配為士伍，給使信家，漸得親近，因賜姓獨孤氏。

translations.literal: His father Tun followed Emperor Shenwu of Qi in battle with Zhou troops at Shayuan; the Qi army was defeated, and he was captured by the pillar of state Dugu Xin, assigned as a common soldier to serve in Xin's household, gradually won closeness, and was granted the surname Dugu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tun fought for Qi Emperor Shenwu against Zhou forces at Shayuan; after Qi's defeat he was captured by Pillar of State Dugu Xin, assigned as a household servant, won Xin's trust over time, and was granted the surname Dugu.

sentences.zh: 楷少謹厚，便弄馬槊，為宇文護執刀，累轉車騎將軍。

translations.literal: Kai in youth was cautious and honest, skilled with horse and lance, served as blade-bearer for Yuwen Hu, and was repeatedly transferred until he became General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Kai was cautious and honest as a youth, skilled with horse and lance, served as Yuwen Hu's bodyguard, and rose to General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 其後數從征伐，賜爵廣阿縣公，邑千戶，拜右侍下大夫。

translations.literal: Afterward he followed several campaigns, was ennobled as Duke of Guang'a county with a fief of a thousand households, and appointed Right Attendant Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in several campaigns, was created Duke of Guang'a with a fief of a thousand households, and appointed Right Attendant Grandee.

sentences.zh: 週末，從韋孝寬平淮南，以功賜子景雲爵西河縣公。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhou he followed Wei Xiaokuan in pacifying Huainan and, for merit, his son Jingyun was ennobled as Duke of Xihe county.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Zhou he followed Wei Xiaokuan in pacifying Huainan, and his son Jingyun was created Duke of Xihe for his father's service.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，進授開府，每督親信兵。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was chief minister, Kai was advanced to Commander-in-Chief and regularly commanded trusted troops.
translations.idiomatic: While Gaozu was chief minister, Kai was made Commander-in-Chief and regularly led the trusted guard.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，拜右監門將軍，進封汝陽郡公。

translations.literal: When the abdication was received, he was appointed General of the Right Gate Guards and advanced to Duke of Ruyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Kai was made General of the Right Gate Guards and enfeoffed as Duke of Ruyang.

sentences.zh: 數歲，遷右衛將軍。

translations.literal: Several years later he was transferred to General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was transferred to General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，出為原州總管。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Renshou he went out as regional commander of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Renshou era he was posted as regional commander of Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 時蜀王秀鎮益州，上征之，猶豫未發。

translations.literal: At the time Prince of Shu Xiu held Yizhou; the emperor was summoning him but hesitated to set out.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shu Xiu was then stationed in Yizhou; the emperor had ordered him to court but hesitated to act.

sentences.zh: 朝廷恐秀生變，拜楷益州總管，馳傳代之。

translations.literal: The court feared Xiu would rebel; Kai was appointed regional commander of Yizhou and hurried by post relay to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Xiu might rebel, the court appointed Kai regional commander of Yizhou and sent him post-haste to replace him.

sentences.zh: 秀果有異志，楷諷諭久之，乃就路。

translations.literal: Xiu indeed harbored rebellious intent; Kai admonished and persuaded him for a long time before he set out on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu did harbor rebellious intent; Kai admonished him at length before he finally set out for the capital.

sentences.zh: 楷察秀有悔色，因勒兵為備。

translations.literal: Kai perceived that Xiu showed regret and therefore drew up his troops on guard.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing regret on Xiu's face, Kai kept his troops under arms as a precaution.

sentences.zh: 秀至興樂，去益州四十餘裡，將反襲楷，密令左右覘所為，知楷不可犯而止。

translations.literal: When Xiu reached Xingle, still more than forty li from Yizhou, he was about to turn back and surprise Kai; he secretly ordered his attendants to observe Kai's conduct, learned that Kai could not be taken lightly, and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: At Xingle, still more than forty li from Yizhou, Xiu was about to turn and attack Kai; he sent men to spy on him, found Kai too formidable to challenge, and gave up the plan.

sentences.zh: 楷在益州，甚有惠政，蜀中父老於今稱之。

translations.literal: Kai in Yizhou had very benevolent administration, and the elders of Shu still praise him to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Kai governed Yizhou with great kindness, and the elders of Shu still speak of him with praise.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，轉并州總管。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang acceded, Kai was transferred to regional commander of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Kai was transferred to regional commander of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 遇疾喪明，上表乞骸骨。

translations.literal: He fell ill and lost his sight, and memorialized asking to retire.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill and lost his sight, then memorialized asking to retire.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「公先朝舊臣，曆職二代，高風素望，臥以鎮之，無勞躬親簿領也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Sir, you are an old minister of the former court, having served through two reigns; your lofty conduct and long-standing repute can secure the region even in repose—there is no need for you personally to handle ledgers and registers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You are a veteran of two reigns, renowned for your integrity; your presence alone will secure the region—you need not trouble yourself with daily paperwork.

sentences.zh: 」遣其長子淩雲監省郡事。

translations.literal: " He sent Kai's eldest son Lingyun to oversee and administer the commandery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent Kai's eldest son Lingyun to supervise the commandery in his stead.

sentences.zh: 其見重如此。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 數載，轉長平太守，未視事而卒。

translations.literal: Several years later he was transferred to administrator of Changping but died before taking up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was appointed administrator of Changping but died before assuming office.

sentences.zh: 諡曰恭。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Gong [Respectful].
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Gong.

sentences.zh: 子淩雲、平雲，彥雲，皆知名。

translations.literal: His sons Lingyun, Pingyun, and Yanyun were all well known.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Lingyun, Pingyun, and Yanyun all achieved renown.

sentences.zh: 楷弟盛，見《誠節傳》。

translations.literal: Kai's younger brother Sheng is treated in the Biography of Loyal Martyrs.
translations.idiomatic: Kai's younger brother Sheng is treated in the Biography of Loyal Martyrs.

sentences.zh: 乞伏慧乞伏慧，字令和，馬邑鮮卑人也。

translations.literal: Qi Fuhui—Qi Fuhui, courtesy name Linghe, was a Xianbei of Mayi.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Fuhui, courtesy name Linghe, was a Xianbei from Mayi.

sentences.zh: 祖周，魏銀青光祿大夫，父纂，金紫光祿大夫，並為第一領民酋長。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhou was Silver Radiance Grand Master of Wei; his father Zuan was Golden Radiance Grand Master; both were chieftains of the first rank among the settled peoples.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhou was a Silver Radiance Grand Master of Wei; his father Zuan was a Golden Radiance Grand Master; both were first-rank tribal chieftains.

sentences.zh: 慧少慷慨有大節，便弓馬，好鷹犬。

translations.literal: Hui in youth was generous and possessed of great integrity, skilled with bow and horse, and fond of hawks and hounds.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Hui was openhanded and high-minded, skilled in archery and horsemanship, and devoted to falconry and hunting.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄帝時，為行台左丞，加蕩寇將軍，累遷右衛將軍、太僕卿，自永甯縣公封宜民郡王。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Wenxiang of Qi he was Left Assistant Director of the Field Office, additionally made General Who Sweeps Away Bandits, and successively promoted to General of the Right Guard and Minister of the Stud; from Duke of Yongning county he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yimin commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi Emperor Wenxiang he served as Left Assistant Director of the Field Office and General Who Sweeps Away Bandits, rose to General of the Right Guard and Minister of the Stud, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Yimin after holding the title Duke of Yongning.

sentences.zh: 其兄貴和又以軍功為王，一門二王，稱為貴顯。

translations.literal: His elder brother Guihe also became a prince through military merit; one household with two princes was called eminent and illustrious.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Guihe also became a prince through military merit; with two princes in one family they were accounted supremely eminent.

sentences.zh: 周武平齊，授使持節、開府儀同大將軍，拜佽飛右旅下大夫，轉熊渠中大夫。

translations.literal: When Zhou Emperor Wu pacified Qi, Hui was granted Bearer of the Staff and Grand Master Commander-in-Chief with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, appointed Junior Grandee of the Right Wing of the Rapid-as-Flying Guard, and transferred to Grandee of the Xiongqu [Bear-brigade] Regiment.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Emperor Wu conquered Qi, Hui was made Bearer of the Staff and Grand Master Commander-in-Chief, appointed Junior Grandee of the Right Wing of the Rapid-as-Flying Guard, and later transferred to Grandee of the Xiongqu Regiment.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，從韋孝寬擊尉惇于武陟，所當皆破，授大將軍，賜物八百段。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was chief minister, he followed Wei Xiaokuan in attacking Yuwen Dun at Wuzhi; wherever he faced the enemy he prevailed, and he was appointed Grand General and granted eight hundred bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: While Gaozu was chief minister, he followed Wei Xiaokuan against Yuwen Dun at Wuzhi, was victorious in every engagement, was made Grand General, and received eight hundred bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 及平尉迥，進位柱國，賜爵西河郡公，邑三千戶，賚物二千三百段。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Yong was pacified, he was advanced to Pillar of State, ennobled as Duke of Xihe commandery with a fief of three thousand households, and granted two thousand three hundred bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuwen Yong's rebellion was crushed, he was made Pillar of State, created Duke of Xihe with a fief of three thousand households, and given two thousand three hundred bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 請以官爵讓兄，朝廷不許，論者義之。

translations.literal: He asked to yield his rank and title to his elder brother; the court did not permit it, but commentators praised his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to yield his rank and title to his elder brother; the court refused, but commentators praised his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，拜曹州刺史。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, Hui was appointed prefect of Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Hui was appointed prefect of Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 曹土舊俗，民多奸隱，戶口名簿帳，恆不以實。

translations.literal: By old custom in Cao territory the people often concealed wrongdoing; household registers and name rolls were habitually not truthful.
translations.idiomatic: Cao had long been a place where people concealed households and falsified registers.

sentences.zh: 慧下車按察，得戶數萬。

translations.literal: When Hui took office he investigated and uncovered tens of thousands of households.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office Hui conducted an investigation and registered tens of thousands of hidden households.

sentences.zh: 遷涼州總管。

translations.literal: He was transferred to regional commander of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to regional commander of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，突厥屢為寇抄，慧於是嚴警烽燧，遠為斥候，虜亦素憚其名，竟不入境。

translations.literal: Earlier the Turks had repeatedly raided; Hui now strictly alerted beacon towers, posted distant scouts, and the enemy had long feared his name—in the end they did not enter the border.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks had raided repeatedly; Hui tightened the beacon system and posted distant scouts, and because they had long feared his name, they never crossed the border.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，轉齊州刺史，得隱戶數千。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to prefect of Qizhou and uncovered several thousand concealed households.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was transferred to Qizhou as prefect and uncovered several thousand hidden households.

sentences.zh: 遷壽州總管。

translations.literal: He was transferred to regional commander of Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to regional commander of Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 其年，左轉杞州刺史，在職數年，遷徐州總管。

translations.literal: That same year he was transferred left to prefect of Qizhou [Qi prefecture]; after several years in office he was moved to regional commander of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was demoted to prefect of Qi prefecture; after several years he was transferred to regional commander of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時年逾七十，上表求致仕，不許。

translations.literal: By then he was over seventy and memorialized asking to retire; permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: By then he was over seventy and asked to retire, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 俄轉荊州總管，又領潭、桂二州總管三十一州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to regional commander of Jingzhou and additionally held military authority over thirty-one prefectures as commander of Tan and Gui [prefectures].
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Jingzhou and given military authority over thirty-one prefectures as commander of Tan and Gui.

sentences.zh: 其俗輕剽，慧躬行樸素以矯之，風化大洽。

translations.literal: The local custom was frivolous and violent; Hui personally practiced plain simplicity to correct it, and customs were greatly harmonized.
translations.idiomatic: The region was lawless and volatile; Hui set an example of plain living and reformed the customs thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 曾見人以穀捕魚者，出絹買而放之，其仁心如此。

translations.literal: Once he saw someone using grain to catch fish; he paid out silk to buy the fish and released them—such was his benevolent heart.
translations.idiomatic: Once he saw a man using grain as bait to catch fish; he paid silk to buy the catch and set the fish free—such was his kindness.

sentences.zh: 百姓美之，號其處曰西河公穀。

translations.literal: The people praised him and called that place Duke of Xihe's Grain.
translations.idiomatic: The people praised him and named the place Duke of Xihe's Grain.

sentences.zh: 轉秦州總管。

translations.literal: He was transferred to regional commander of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to regional commander of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，為天水太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang acceded, Hui became administrator of Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Hui became administrator of Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 大業五年，征吐谷渾，郡濱西境，民苦勞役，又遇帝西巡，坐為道不整，獻食疏薄，帝大怒，命左右斬之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daye, during the campaign against Tuyuhun, the commandery bordered the western frontier; the people suffered under corvée labor, and when the emperor toured westward, Hui was charged because the road was not in order and the food offered was meager; the emperor was furious and ordered his attendants to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Daye, during the campaign against Tuyuhun, his commandery lay on the western frontier where the people were exhausted by labor levies; when the emperor passed westward, Hui was blamed because the road was not ready and the provisions were poor; the emperor was enraged and ordered him executed.

sentences.zh: 見其無發，乃釋，除名為民。

translations.literal: Seeing that he had no hair, the emperor released him, stripped his name and rank, and made him a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that he was bald, the emperor spared him but stripped him of rank and made him a commoner.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 張威張威，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Wei—Zhang Wei was of unknown origin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wei was of unknown origin.

sentences.zh: 父琛，魏弘農太守。

translations.literal: His father Chen was administrator of Hongnong in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chen had been administrator of Hongnong under the Wei.

sentences.zh: 威少倜儻有大志，善騎射，膂力過人。

translations.literal: Wei in youth was free-spirited and ambitious, skilled in mounted archery, and his physical strength surpassed other men.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Wei was bold and ambitious, excelled at horseback archery, and possessed extraordinary strength.

sentences.zh: 在周，數從征伐，位至柱國、京兆尹，封長壽縣公，邑千戶。

translations.literal: Under Zhou he followed several campaigns, rose to Pillar of State and Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Changshou county with a fief of a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou he campaigned repeatedly, rose to Pillar of State and Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, and was created Duke of Changshou with a fief of a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 王謙作亂，高祖以威為行軍總管，從元帥梁睿擊之。

translations.literal: When Wang Qian rebelled, Gaozu made Wei campaign commander to follow the commander-in-chief Liang Rui in attacking him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Qian rebelled, Gaozu appointed Wei campaign commander under Marshal Liang Rui to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 軍次通穀，謙守將李三王擁勁兵拒守，睿以威為先鋒。

translations.literal: The army halted at Tonggu; Qian's defending general Li Sanwang held strong troops in defense, and Rui made Wei vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Tonggu, where Qian's defender Li Sanwang held the pass with elite troops; Rui made Wei his vanguard.

sentences.zh: 三王初閉壘不戰，威令人詈侮以激怒之，三王果出陣。

translations.literal: Sanwang at first closed the stockade and would not fight; Wei had men revile and insult him to provoke anger, and Sanwang indeed came out to battle.
translations.idiomatic: Sanwang at first refused battle behind his walls; Wei had men taunt and insult him until Sanwang came out to fight.

sentences.zh: 威令壯士奮擊，三王軍潰，大兵繼至，於是擒斬四千餘人。

translations.literal: Wei ordered stalwarts to strike fiercely; Sanwang's army collapsed, the main force followed up, and more than four thousand were captured and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Wei sent his best fighters forward; Sanwang's army broke, the main force followed, and more than four thousand were killed or captured.

sentences.zh: 進至開遠，謙將趙儼眾十萬，連營三十裡。

translations.literal: Advancing to Kaiyuan, Qian's general Zhao Yan had a host of a hundred thousand with camps strung for thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to Kaiyuan, they faced Qian's general Zhao Yan with a hundred thousand men in camps stretching thirty li.

sentences.zh: 威鑿山通道，自西嶺攻其背，儼遂敗走。

translations.literal: Wei cut a passage through the mountain, attacked from the western ridge against their rear, and Yan was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wei cut a path through the mountains, struck from the western ridge against their rear, and Yan was routed.

sentences.zh: 追至成都，與謙大戰，威將中軍。

translations.literal: Pursuing to Chengdu, they fought a great battle with Qian; Wei commanded the center army.
translations.idiomatic: They pursued to Chengdu and fought a great battle with Qian; Wei commanded the center.

sentences.zh: 及謙平，進位上柱國，拜瀘州總管。

translations.literal: When Qian was pacified, Wei was advanced to Senior Pillar of State and appointed regional commander of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Qian's defeat Wei was promoted to Senior Pillar of State and appointed regional commander of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，曆幽、洛二州總管，改封晉熙郡公。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, Wei successively served as regional commander of You and Luo [prefectures] and his fief was changed to Duke of Jinxi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Wei served as regional commander of You and Luozhou in turn and was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Jinxi.

sentences.zh: 尋拜河北道行台僕射，後督晉王軍府事。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Vice Director of the Hebei Circuit Field Office, and later supervised the military headquarters of Prince Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Vice Director of the Hebei Circuit Field Office and later supervised Prince Jin's military headquarters.

sentences.zh: 數年，拜青州總管，賜錢八十萬，米五百石，雜彩三百段。

translations.literal: Several years later he was appointed regional commander of Qingzhou and granted eight hundred thousand cash, five hundred piculs of grain, and three hundred bolts of mixed silks.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was appointed regional commander of Qingzhou and given eight hundred thousand cash, five hundred piculs of grain, and three hundred bolts of silks.

sentences.zh: 威在青州，頗治產業，遣家奴于民間鬻蘆菔根，其奴緣此侵擾百姓。

translations.literal: Wei in Qingzhou greatly built up estates and sent household slaves among the people to sell radish roots; the slaves on this account harassed the common people.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingzhou Wei built up his estates and sent household slaves to sell radish roots among the people; the slaves used this as a pretext to harass the populace.

sentences.zh: 上深加譴責，坐廢於家。

translations.literal: The emperor sternly rebuked him, and he was dismissed and confined at home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked him severely and dismissed him to his home.

sentences.zh: 後從上祠太山，至洛陽，上謂威曰：「自朕之有天下，每委公以重鎮，可謂推赤心矣。

translations.literal: Later, following the emperor in sacrificing at Mount Tai and arriving at Luoyang, the emperor said to Wei: "Since I gained the realm, I have repeatedly entrusted you with vital posts—truly I have offered you my open heart.
translations.idiomatic: Later, accompanying the emperor to sacrifice at Mount Tai and reaching Luoyang, the emperor said to Wei, "Since I gained the realm I have repeatedly entrusted you with vital posts—I have given you my full trust.

sentences.zh: 何乃不修名行，唯利是視？

translations.literal: Why then do you not cultivate reputation and conduct, but look only to profit?
translations.idiomatic: Why then have you neglected your reputation and looked only to profit?

sentences.zh: 豈直孤負朕心，亦且累卿名德。

translations.literal: This not only betrays my heart but also mars your own fame and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: You have not only failed me but also stained your own good name.

sentences.zh: 」因問威曰：「公所執笏今安在？

translations.literal: " He then asked Wei: "Where is the tablet you used to hold at court?
translations.idiomatic: " He then asked, "Where is the court tablet you once carried?

sentences.zh: 」威頓首曰：「臣負罪虧憲，無顏複執，謹藏於家。

translations.literal: " Wei bowed his head and said: "Your servant has committed offense and fallen short of the statutes; I have no face to hold it again and have respectfully kept it at home.
translations.idiomatic: " Wei bowed low and said, "I have offended and broken the law; I am ashamed to hold it again and have kept it at home.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「可持來。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Bring it here.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Bring it tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 」威明日奉笏以見，上曰：「公雖不遵法度，功效實多，朕不忘之。

translations.literal: " The next day Wei presented the tablet at audience; the emperor said: "Though you did not observe the law, your achievements were many, and I have not forgotten them.
translations.idiomatic: " The next day Wei brought the tablet to court; the emperor said, "Though you broke the law, your service has been great, and I have not forgotten it.

sentences.zh: 今還公笏。

translations.literal: I now return your tablet.
translations.idiomatic: I return your tablet to you now.

sentences.zh: 」於是複拜洛州刺史，後封睆城郡公。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was again appointed prefect of Luozhou and later enfeoffed as Duke of Wancheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: " He was then reappointed prefect of Luozhou and later enfeoffed as Duke of Wancheng.

sentences.zh: 尋轉相州刺史，卒官。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to prefect of Xiangzhou and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Xiangzhou as prefect and died in office.

sentences.zh: 有子植，大業中，至武賁郎將。

translations.literal: He had a son Zhi who, in the Daye era, rose to Commandant of the Martial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhi rose during the Daye era to Commandant of the Martial Guards.

sentences.zh: 和洪和洪，汝南人也。

translations.literal: He Hong—He Hong was a native of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: He Hong was from Runan.

sentences.zh: 少有武力，勇烈過人。

translations.literal: In youth he had martial prowess; his courage and fierceness surpassed other men.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was physically powerful, and his courage exceeded that of ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 周武帝時，數從征伐，以戰功累遷車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Wu of Zhou he followed several campaigns and, for battle merit, was repeatedly promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Palace Attendant of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou Emperor Wu he campaigned repeatedly and, for his victories, rose to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Palace Attendant of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 時龍州蠻任公忻、李國立等聚眾為亂，刺史獨孤善不能禦。

translations.literal: At the time the barbarians of Longzhou, Ren Gongxin, Li Guoli, and others gathered crowds in rebellion; the prefect Dugu Shan could not repel them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Longzhou tribesmen Ren Gongxin and Li Guoli gathered forces in rebellion, and Prefect Dugu Shan could not suppress them.

sentences.zh: 朝議以洪有武略，代善為刺史。

translations.literal: The court deliberated that Hong had military talent and replaced Shan as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: The court decided that Hong had military talent and replaced Shan as prefect.

sentences.zh: 月餘，擒公忻、國立，皆斬首梟之，餘党悉平。

translations.literal: After more than a month he captured Gongxin and Guoli, beheaded them both and displayed their heads, and the remaining partisans were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he captured Gongxin and Guoli, executed them and displayed their heads, and pacified the remaining rebels.

sentences.zh: 從帝攻河陰，洪力戰，陷其西門。

translations.literal: Following the emperor in attacking Heyin, Hong fought fiercely and stormed the western gate.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the emperor in the attack on Heyin, fought fiercely, and took the western gate.

sentences.zh: 帝壯之，賞物千段。

translations.literal: The emperor admired him and rewarded him with a thousand bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was impressed and rewarded him with a thousand bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 複從帝平齊，進位上儀同，賜爵北平侯，邑八百戶，拜左勳曹下大夫。

translations.literal: He again followed the emperor in pacifying Qi, was advanced to Senior Palace Attendant of the First Rank, ennobled as Marquis of Beiping with a fief of eight hundred households, and appointed Junior Grandee of the Left Merit Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed the emperor in the conquest of Qi, was promoted to Senior Palace Attendant of the First Rank, created Marquis of Beiping with eight hundred households, and appointed Junior Grandee of the Left Merit Bureau.

sentences.zh: 柱國王軌之擒吳明徹也，洪有功焉，加位開府，遷折衝中大夫。

translations.literal: When the pillar of state Wang Gui captured Wu Mingche, Hong had merit therein; he was additionally made Commander-in-Chief and transferred to Grandee of the Break-the-Ranks Regiment.
translations.idiomatic: When Pillar of State Wang Gui captured Wu Mingche, Hong distinguished himself and was made Commander-in-Chief and transferred to Grandee of the Break-the-Ranks Regiment.

sentences.zh: 尉迥作亂相州，以洪為行軍總管，從韋孝寬擊之。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Yong rebelled at Xiangzhou, Hong was made campaign commander to follow Wei Xiaokuan in attacking him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Yong rebelled at Xiangzhou, Hong was appointed campaign commander under Wei Xiaokuan.

sentences.zh: 軍至河陽，迥遣兵圍懷州，洪與總管宇文述等擊走。

translations.literal: When the army reached Heyang, Yong sent troops to besiege Huaizhou; Hong with regional commander Yuwen Shu and others drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: At Heyang, Yong sent troops to besiege Huaizhou; Hong and Regional Commander Yuwen Shu drove them off.

sentences.zh: 又破尉惇于武陟。

translations.literal: He again defeated Yuwen Dun at Wuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He also defeated Yuwen Dun at Wuzhi.

sentences.zh: 及平相州，每戰有功，拜柱國，封廣武郡公，邑二千戶。

translations.literal: When Xiangzhou was pacified, he had merit in every battle; he was appointed Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Duke of Guangwu commandery with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiangzhou fell he distinguished himself in every battle, was made Pillar of State, and was created Duke of Guangwu with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 前後賜物萬段，奴婢五十口，金銀各百挺，牛馬百匹。

translations.literal: Before and after he was granted ten thousand bolts of goods, fifty household slaves, a hundred ingots each of gold and silver, and a hundred head of cattle and horses.
translations.idiomatic: In all he received ten thousand bolts of goods, fifty slaves, a hundred ingots each of gold and silver, and a hundred head of cattle and horses.

sentences.zh: 時東夏初平，物情尚梗，高祖以洪有威名，令領冀州事，甚得人和。

translations.literal: At the time eastern Xia had just been pacified and popular sentiment was still unsettled; Gaozu, because Hong had a formidable reputation, ordered him to take charge of Jizhou affairs, and he won great harmony among the people.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern China had only just been pacified and the region was still unsettled; Gaozu put Hong in charge of Jizhou for his renown, and he won the people's trust.

sentences.zh: 數歲，征入朝，為漕渠總管監，轉拜泗州刺史。

translations.literal: Several years later he was summoned to court, served as supervisor of the Grand Canal commandery, and was transferred to prefect of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was recalled to court, supervised the Grand Canal administration, and was transferred to Sizhou as prefect.

sentences.zh: 屬突厥寇邊，詔洪為北道行軍總管，擊走虜，至磧而還。

translations.literal: When the Turks raided the frontier, Hong was ordered as campaign commander of the northern route; he drove off the enemy and returned upon reaching the desert.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks raided the frontier, Hong was made northern campaign commander, drove them off, and returned after reaching the desert.

sentences.zh: 後遷徐州總管，卒，時年六十四。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to regional commander of Xuzhou and died at the age of sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to regional commander of Xuzhou and died at sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 侯莫陳穎侯莫陳穎，字遵道，代人也。

translations.literal: Houmo Chenying—Houmo Chenying, courtesy name Zundao, was a native of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Houmo Chenying, courtesy name Zundao, was from Dai.

sentences.zh: 與魏南遷，世為列將。

translations.literal: Moving south with Wei, his family for generations were ranking generals.
translations.idiomatic: His family moved south with the Wei and for generations served as field commanders.

sentences.zh: 父崇，魏、周之際，曆職顯要，官至大司空。

translations.literal: His father Chong, between Wei and Zhou, held prominent posts in succession and rose to Grand Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chong held high office during the transition from Wei to Zhou and rose to Grand Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 穎少有器量，風神警發，為時輩所推。

translations.literal: Ying in youth had capacity and breadth of mind, a spirited and alert bearing, and was promoted by men of his generation.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Ying was broad-minded and keen of bearing, and his contemporaries held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 魏大統末，以父軍功賜爵廣平侯，累遷開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the end of Great Dominion in Wei he was ennobled as Marquis of Guangping for his father's military merit and was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Wei Great Dominion era he was created Marquis of Guangping for his father's service and rose to Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 周武帝時，從滕王逌擊龍泉、文城叛胡，與柱國豆盧勣各帥兵分路而進。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Wu of Zhou he followed Prince of Teng Yu in attacking the rebel Hu of Longquan and Wencheng; he and the pillar of state Doulu Ji each led troops by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou Emperor Wu he followed Prince of Teng Yu against the rebel Hu of Longquan and Wencheng, advancing by separate routes with Pillar of State Doulu Ji.

sentences.zh: 穎懸軍五百餘裡，破其三柵。

translations.literal: Ying led his army deep for more than five hundred li and broke three of their stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Ying marched more than five hundred li into enemy territory and captured three stockades.

sentences.zh: 先是，稽胡叛亂，輒略邊人為奴婢。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Ji Hu rebelled, they regularly seized frontier people as slaves.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, whenever the Ji Hu rebelled, they seized frontier people as slaves.

sentences.zh: 至是詔胡敢有壓匿良人者誅，籍沒其妻子。

translations.literal: At this time an edict declared that any Hu who dared conceal commoners should be executed and his wife and children registered and confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: An edict now declared that any Hu who concealed commoners would be executed and his family confiscated.

sentences.zh: 有人言為胡村所隱匿者，勣將誅之，穎謂勣曰：「將在外，君命有所不行。

translations.literal: Someone said concealed persons were hidden in a Hu village; Ji was about to execute them, and Ying said to Ji: "When the general is abroad, the ruler's command may in part go unheeded.
translations.idiomatic: When someone reported that commoners were hidden in a Hu village, Ji was about to execute the villagers; Ying told him, "A general in the field is not bound to obey every command from court.

sentences.zh: 諸胡固非悉反，但相迫脅為亂耳。

translations.literal: These Hu are certainly not all in rebellion; they have merely been compelled and coerced into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Not all the Hu have rebelled; most were forced into it.

sentences.zh: 大兵臨之，首亂者知懼，脅從者思降。

translations.literal: When great armies press upon them, the ringleaders will know fear and those coerced will think of surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When our armies advance, the ringleaders will fear for their lives and the followers will wish to surrender.

sentences.zh: 今漸加撫慰，自可不戰而定。

translations.literal: If we now gradually add reassurance and comfort, we can secure the matter without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: If we reassure them gradually, we can settle this without a battle.

sentences.zh: 如即誅之，轉相驚恐，為難不細。

translations.literal: If we execute them at once, they will in turn be alarmed and terrified, and the trouble will be no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: If we execute them now, we will only spread panic and make the trouble far worse.

sentences.zh: 未若召其渠帥，以隱匿者付之，令自歸首，則群胡可安。
