translations.literal: Better to summon their chieftains, hand over the concealed persons to them, and order them to surrender of their own accord—then the Hu masses can be pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Better to summon their chieftains, hand the concealed persons over to them, and let them surrender voluntarily—the Hu will then be pacified.

sentences.zh: 」勣從之。

translations.literal: " Ji followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Ji followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 群胡感悅，爭來降附，北土以安。

translations.literal: The Hu masses were moved and pleased and vied to come and submit; the northern lands were thereby secure.
translations.idiomatic: The Hu were grateful and submitted in great numbers, and the north was pacified.

sentences.zh: 遷司武，加振威中大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of Martial Affairs and additionally made Grandee of the Shake-the-Foe Regiment.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Director of Martial Affairs and made Grandee of the Shake-the-Foe Regiment.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，拜昌州刺史。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was chief minister, Ying was appointed prefect of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: While Gaozu was chief minister, Ying was appointed prefect of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 會受禪，竟不行，加上開府，進爵升平郡公。

translations.literal: Just as the abdication was received, he in the end did not take up the post; he was additionally made Senior Commander-in-Chief and advanced to Duke of Shengping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne he never assumed that post; instead he was made Senior Commander-in-Chief and created Duke of Shengping.

sentences.zh: 俄拜延州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 數年，轉陳州刺史。

translations.literal: Several years later he was transferred to prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was transferred to Chenzhou as prefect.

sentences.zh: 平陳之役，以行軍總管從秦王俊出魯山道。

translations.literal: In the campaign to pacify Chen, as campaign commander he followed Prince of Qin Jun out by the Lushan route.
translations.idiomatic: In the conquest of Chen he served as campaign commander under Prince of Qin Yang Jun, advancing by the Lushan route.

sentences.zh: 屬陳將荀法尚、陳紀降，穎與行軍總管段文振度江安集初附。

translations.literal: When the Chen generals Xun Fashang and Chen Ji surrendered, Ying with campaign commander Duan Wenzhen crossed the river to settle and gather those who had just submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chen generals Xun Fashang and Chen Ji surrendered, Ying and Campaign Commander Duan Wenzhen crossed the Yangzi to settle the newly submitted territories.

sentences.zh: 尋拜饒州刺史，未之官，遷瀛州刺史，甚有惠政。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed prefect of Raozhou but did not take office; he was transferred to prefect of Yingzhou, where he had very benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed to Raozhou but never took office; transferred to Yingzhou, he governed with notable kindness.

sentences.zh: 在職數年，坐與秦王俊交通免官。

translations.literal: During several years in office he was dismissed for communicating with Prince of Qin Jun.
translations.idiomatic: After several years in office he was dismissed for associating with Prince of Qin Yang Jun.

sentences.zh: 百姓將送者，莫不流涕，因相與立碑，頌穎清德。

translations.literal: Among the common people who came to see him off, none failed to weep; they together erected a stele praising Ying's pure virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The people who came to see him off wept openly, and together they erected a stele praising his integrity.

sentences.zh: 未幾，檢校汾州事，俄拜邢州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was put in provisional charge of Fenzhou affairs, and soon appointed prefect of Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was put in provisional charge of Fenzhou and shortly afterward appointed prefect of Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，吏部尚書牛弘持節巡撫山東，以穎為第一。

translations.literal: During Renshou, Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Niu Hong, bearing the staff, toured and pacified Shandong and ranked Ying first.
translations.idiomatic: During Renshou, Minister of Personnel Niu Hong toured Shandong with imperial authority and ranked Ying first among the officials.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘉歎，優詔褒揚。

translations.literal: Gaozu praised and sighed over this and issued an excellent edict commending him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu expressed his admiration and issued a gracious edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷以嶺南刺史、縣令多貪鄙，蠻夷怨叛，妙簡清吏以鎮撫之，於是征穎入朝。

translations.literal: At the time the court considered that prefects and county magistrates in Lingnan were mostly greedy and base, and the barbarians resented and rebelled; they carefully selected upright officials to pacify them, and so Ying was summoned to court.
translations.idiomatic: The court believed that Lingnan officials were mostly corrupt and that the tribes were rebelling; it sought upright administrators to pacify the region and summoned Ying to court.

sentences.zh: 及進見，上與穎言及平生，以為歡笑。

translations.literal: When he was received in audience, the emperor spoke with Ying of their lives and took it as mirth.
translations.idiomatic: At his audience the emperor spoke with him of old times and they shared a warm laugh.

sentences.zh: 數日，進位大將軍，拜桂州總管十七州諸軍事，賜物而遣之。

translations.literal: Several days later he was advanced to Grand General, appointed regional commander of Guizhou with military authority over seventeen prefectures, granted goods, and sent forth.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later he was promoted to Grand General, appointed regional commander of Guizhou with authority over seventeen prefectures, given gifts, and sent south.

sentences.zh: 及到官，大崇恩信，民夷悅服，溪洞生越，多來歸附。

translations.literal: When he reached his post he greatly promoted favor and trust; Chinese and barbarians submitted gladly, and many raw Yue from stream caves came to attach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he won people with kindness and trust; Chinese and tribesmen alike submitted gladly, and many Yue from the hill country came to pledge allegiance.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，穎兄梁國公芮坐事徙邊，朝廷恐穎不自安，征歸京師。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang acceded, Ying's elder brother the Duke of Liang Rui was banished to the frontier for an offense; the court feared Ying would not feel secure and summoned him back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Ying's elder brother Duke of Liang Rui was banished for an offense; fearing Ying might be unsettled, the court recalled him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 數年，拜恆山太守。

translations.literal: Several years later he was appointed administrator of Hengshan.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was appointed administrator of Hengshan.

sentences.zh: 其年，嶺南、閩越多不附，帝以穎前在桂州有惠政，為南土所信伏，複拜南海太守。

translations.literal: That same year Lingnan and the Min-Yue regions largely did not submit; the emperor, because Ying had earlier had benevolent administration in Guizhou and was trusted and revered in the southern lands, again appointed him administrator of Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: That year Lingnan and Min-Yue were largely in revolt; because Ying's earlier rule in Guizhou had won the south's trust, the emperor reappointed him administrator of Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 後四歲，卒官。

translations.literal: Four years later he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later he died in office.

sentences.zh: 諡曰定。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Ding [Settled].
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Ding.

sentences.zh: 子虔會，最知名。

translations.literal: His son Qianhui was the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qianhui became the most famous of his descendants.

sentences.zh: 【論】史臣曰：杜彥東夏、南服，屢有戰功，作鎮朔垂，胡塵不起。

translations.literal: [Commentary] The historiographer says: Du Yan in eastern Xia and the southern domains repeatedly had battle merit; holding the northern frontier, Turkic dust did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: [Commentary] The historian writes: Du Yan won repeated victories in the east and south; on the northern frontier he kept the barbarians at bay.

sentences.zh: 高勱死亡之際，志氣懍然，疾彼奸邪，致茲餘慶。

translations.literal: Gao Mai at the moment of Qi's fall had stern and unyielding spirit, hated those wicked and devious men, and thereby brought down this remaining blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Mai faced Qi's fall with unbroken spirit, condemned its wicked ministers, and left his house a legacy of honor.

sentences.zh: 爾硃敞幼有權奇，終能止足，崇基墜而複構，不亦仁且智乎！

translations.literal: Erzhu Chang in youth had resourceful strangeness and in the end knew when to stop; a lofty foundation fell and was built again—is this not both benevolent and wise!
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Chang showed early resourcefulness and knew when to stop; his house fell and rose again—was this not wisdom joined to humanity!

sentences.zh: 周搖以質實見知，獨孤以恤人流譽，乞伏慧能以國讓，侯莫陳所居治理，或知牧人之道，或踐仁義之路，皆有可稱焉。

translations.literal: Zhou Yao was known for plain substance, Dugu for compassion toward the people, Qi Fuhui for ability to yield rank and state, and Houmo Chen for good governance wherever he served—some knew the way of shepherding the people, some walked the path of benevolence and righteousness; all had what may be praised.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yao was valued for integrity, Dugu Kai for compassion, Qi Fuhui for yielding honors to his brother, and Houmo Chenying for good governance—some knew how to rule the people, others walked the path of benevolence; each had qualities worth praise.

sentences.zh: 慧以供帳不厚，至於放黜，並結髮登朝，出入三代，終享祿位，不夭性齡，蓋其任心而行，不為矯飾之所致也。

translations.literal: Hui because his provisions and equipage were not lavish was even dismissed from office; yet all from youth entered court, passed through three dynasties, and in the end enjoyed salary and rank without shortened natural span—probably because they acted as their hearts directed and did not owe it to forced ornamentation.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was dismissed because his official hospitality was too plain; yet they all entered service young, served three dynasties, and died in honor at full span—because they acted from the heart and never put on airs.
